Research Paper Title: HCiT: Deepfake Video Detection Using a Hybrid CNN + Vision Transformer Model
Journal / Conference Name: IEEE VCIP (Int. Conf. Visual Communication & Image Processing), Munich
Problem / Objective: Combine local texture features (CNN) with global attention features (ViT) for improved deepfake video detection
Methodology Adopted: Hybrid CNN + Vision Transformer (HCiT) — CNN extracts local spatial features; ViT captures global attention patterns
Limitations: Higher compute cost than pure CNN; limited to face-swap manipulations tested on FaceForensics++ and DFDC preview only
Future Enhancements: Extend to other manipulation types (reenactment, audio-visual); reduce Transformer compute overhead

Research Paper Title: A Deepfake Detection Method Based on Transformer Spatiotemporal Modeling (STFormer)*
Journal / Conference Name: IEEE Conference Publication (verify venue on IEEE Xplore)
Problem / Objective: Model both spatial artifacts and temporal inconsistencies in deepfake videos using a pure Transformer architecture
Methodology Adopted: 4-stage pyramid Transformer with Spatiotemporal Embedding Layer + GRU for inter-frame dynamics
Metrics Used: Accuracy, AUC on FaceForensics++ and Celeb-DF
Limitations: Complex multi-stage pipeline; high GPU memory; not tested on heavy compression or real-world social media re-encoding
Future Enhancements: Lightweight distillation; deployment on mobile/edge devices

Research Paper Title: Leveraging Swin Transformer for Robust Deepfake Detection*
Journal / Conference Name: IEEE Conference Publication (verify venue on IEEE Xplore)
Problem / Objective: Improve resilience to unseen/newer manipulation techniques using shifted-window self-attention
Methodology Adopted: Swin Transformer (shifted-window self-attention) fine-tuned for face forensics
Metrics Used: Accuracy, Precision, Recall on LCC-FASD + CASIA combined
Limitations: Evaluated on combined dataset only; no standalone cross-dataset generalization reported; high compute
Future Enhancements: Combine with provenance/blockchain; test on DFDC and Celeb-DF

Research Paper Title: GenConViT: Deepfake Video Detection Using Generative Convolutional Vision Transformer
Problem / Objective: Combine visual artifact detection with latent-distribution modeling for generalized deepfake detection
Methodology Adopted: ConvNeXt + Swin Transformer + Autoencoder/VAE latent-space modeling
Metrics Used: 95.8% avg accuracy, 99.3% AUC across DFDC, FF++, DeepfakeTIMIT, Celeb-DF v2
Limitations: Computationally expensive dual-branch architecture; no real-time deployment demonstrated
Future Enhancements: Real-time optimization; integration with provenance systems

Research Paper Title: Video Deepfake Detection Using EfficientNet and LSTM*
Journal / Conference Name: IRJIET (Int. Res. J. Innovation in Eng. & Tech.)
Problem / Objective: Combine spatial (per-frame) and temporal (inter-frame) analysis for video deepfake detection
Methodology Adopted: EfficientNetB0 spatial encoder + LSTM temporal sequence model
Metrics Used: Accuracy, frame-level precision on face-manipulation video benchmark
Limitations: Single benchmark; no robustness testing under compression/noise; no explainability
Future Enhancements: Add Grad-CAM overlays; test under social media degradations

Research Paper Title: An Enhanced Deep Learning Framework for DeepFake Detection Using EfficientNet-B3
Problem / Objective: Compare deep transfer-learned CNNs against classical ML methods for deepfake image detection
Methodology Adopted: EfficientNet-B3 vs. SVM / Random Forest / ensemble ML classifiers
Limitations: Only image-level classification; no video support; no interpretability/explainability module
Future Enhancements: Add explainability (XAI); extend to video; cross-dataset generalization testing

Research Paper Title: Explainable AI for Deepfake Detection: A Grad-CAM Approach to Video Forensics*
Problem / Objective: Add interpretability to CNN-based video deepfake detection using Grad-CAM heatmaps
Methodology Adopted: EfficientNetB0 + LSTM + Grad-CAM overlay on per-frame predictions
Limitations: Grad-CAM is post-hoc only; no tamper-evident record of the verdict or heatmap; no blockchain
Future Enhancements: Integrate with blockchain anchoring; quantitative XAI evaluation metrics

Research Paper Title: Explainable Deepfake Detection: Integrating Grad-CAM with CNN-RNN Architecture
Problem / Objective: Provide statistically validated explainability alongside deepfake detection
Methodology Adopted: DenseNet-121 + Bidirectional GRU + Grad-CAM
Limitations: Moderate accuracy (88.33%); no blockchain or tamper-proof anchoring of the verdict
Future Enhancements: Improve accuracy with better backbone; add immutable verdict storage

Research Paper Title: Towards Quantitative Evaluation of Explainable AI Methods for Deepfake Detection
Problem / Objective: Develop quantitative metrics to evaluate whether XAI methods (Grad-CAM, LIME) align with actual forgery cues
Methodology Adopted: Comparative evaluation framework across Grad-CAM, LIME, and related XAI methods
Limitations: Shows existing XAI overlays often do NOT align with human-perceived forgery cues; no system proposed
Future Enhancements: Design XAI methods specifically tuned for forensic cues rather than generic saliency

Research Paper Title: Securing Digital Integrity: Comprehensive Framework for Deepfake Detection and Blockchain Validation
Problem / Objective: Combine CNN deepfake detection with Ethereum smart contracts and IPFS for tamper-proof validation
Methodology Adopted: EfficientNet-B1 CNN + Ethereum smart contracts + IPFS content storage
Limitations: No Grad-CAM or visual evidence trail bundled with the on-chain proof; opaque label written on-chain
Future Enhancements: Add explainability (Grad-CAM); PDF certificate generation; robustness benchmarking

Research Paper Title: Blockchain Based Deep Fake Detection and Verification*
Problem / Objective: Combine a CNN detector with Ethereum blockchain for immutable deepfake detection records
Methodology Adopted: CNN detector + Ethereum smart contract + IPFS content identifiers (CIDs)
Metrics Used: Accuracy on image dataset with real/fake labels
Limitations: No visual explanation of the AI verdict; provenance is a hash-only record without evidence trail
Future Enhancements: Integrate XAI; add PDF certificate with visual proof; stress-test robustness

Research Paper Title: A Blockchain-based Framework for Content Provenance and Authenticity*
Journal / Conference Name: Proc. ECAI (16th Int. Conf. Electronics, Computers & AI)
Problem / Objective: Track content provenance and history to an original source using blockchain
Methodology Adopted: Ethereum smart contract + IPFS hash anchoring
Limitations: No AI-based forgery/deepfake classification performed — assumes content is authentic at upload
Future Enhancements: Integrate a deepfake detection model to verify content before anchoring

Research Paper Title: Blockchain Technology for Combating Deepfake and Protect Video/Image Integrity
Journal / Conference Name: J. Korea Multimedia Society, Rashid, Lee & Kwon
Problem / Objective: Trace media to a trusted origin using blockchain and IPFS hashing
Methodology Adopted: Ethereum blockchain + IPFS-hash provenance
Limitations: Foundational framework only; no built-in deepfake classifier; trust anchored at upload time
Future Enhancements: Add automated AI screening before hash registration

Research Paper Title: A Blockchain-Based Secure Framework for Multimedia Content Tracing and Copyright Protection
Journal / Conference Name: IEEE Trans. Industrial Informatics, Li, Wang & Kumari
Problem / Objective: Provide blockchain-based content tracing for copyright protection
Methodology Adopted: Blockchain-based content tracing with access-control mechanisms
Limitations: Focuses only on copyright; does not address AI-generated manipulation/deepfake detection
Future Enhancements: Extend to deepfake detection; combine with AI classification

Research Paper Title: NFTs for Combating Deepfakes and Fake Metaverse Digital Contents*
Problem / Objective: Extend provenance tracking into NFT/metaverse contexts using blockchain
Methodology Adopted: Blockchain + NFTs + IPFS hashing for digital asset provenance
Limitations: Trust anchored only at upload/mint time; no pixel-level forgery analysis
Future Enhancements: Integrate AI deepfake screening before NFT minting

Research Paper Title: Combating Deepfake Videos Using Blockchain and Smart Contracts
Problem / Objective: Prove video authenticity by tracing to a trusted publisher via blockchain
Methodology Adopted: Ethereum smart contracts for source traceability
Limitations: Early proof-of-concept; no AI detection component; if publisher is compromised, trust fails
Future Enhancements: Add automated deepfake detection; scale beyond single-publisher trust model

Research Paper Title: Birds of a Feather: Enhancing Multimodal Fake News Detection via Multi-Element Retrieval (ReTIP)*
Problem / Objective: Overcome knowledge-paucity in multimodal fake news detection by retrieving related content
Methodology Adopted: Retrieval-augmented multimodal (text + image) fusion with multi-element retrieval
Metrics Used: Detection accuracy on social-media multimodal news corpus
Limitations: Not integrated with a verifiable per-asset evidentiary chain; no blockchain/hash anchoring
Future Enhancements: Add per-asset blockchain audit trail; extend to video deepfakes

Research Paper Title: A Comprehensive Review of Deepfake Detection Techniques
Problem / Objective: Systematic review of classical ML, CNN, and Transformer approaches for deepfake detection (2018–2025)
Methodology Adopted: Survey / meta-analysis across 100+ papers
Metrics Used: Cross-dataset generalization drop: Transformers ~11.3% vs CNNs >15%
Limitations: Survey only; no system proposed; identifies generalization and robustness as persistent open gaps
Future Enhancements: Develop systems that address the identified gaps systematically

Research Paper Title: Image Forgery Detection and Localization: A 2016–2025 Survey*
Problem / Objective: Comprehensive taxonomy of image forensics methods (handcrafted, CNN, Transformer)
Methodology Adopted: Survey / taxonomy across handcrafted features, CNN, and Transformer forensics
Metrics Used: Coverage of Columbia, CASIA, NIST16, DEFACTO + 8 benchmarks
Limitations: Flags cross-dataset generalization, compression robustness, and explainability as persistent open challenges
Future Enhancements: Design robust, explainable detectors with systematic degradation benchmarks

Research Paper Title: C2PA Content Credentials Specification
Journal / Conference Name: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA), v2.3
Problem / Objective: Cryptographically sign provenance manifests at content creation/editing time
Methodology Adopted: Cryptographic manifest signing attached to media files at capture/edit
Metrics Used: Industry standard compliance; provenance chain integrity
Limitations: Explicitly does NOT verify the truth of content — an AI generator can sign synthetic media with a 'valid' manifest
Future Enhancements: Integrate with AI-based content verification to check truth, not just provenance
